bullets.title: CRWV: Q2 Blowout — Backlog +250% to $104B+, Stock +20%
bullets.body: CoreWeave surged ~20% after Q2 results showed revenue approximately doubling YoY, backlog surging nearly 250% to $104B+, and $25B+ in new early Q3 commitments. Adjusted EBITDA margin ran at ~59%; Martin Shkreli was vocally short (16% of float short going in) but the print overwhelmed bears. Analysts broadly bullish on AI cloud infrastructure demand.

bullets.title: NBIS: +34% on 454% Revenue Growth, Citi Upgrades to Buy with $278 PT
bullets.body: Nebius Group delivered Q2 revenue of $582M (+454% YoY, +46% QoQ) with adj. EBITDA margin of 40.6% vs. 29.6% consensus. ARR hit $3.0B (+598% YoY); four major AI cloud deals averaged >$1B TCV at $20-25M ACV/MW with sub-2-year paybacks. FY26 guidance reiterated at $3.0-3.4B revenue. Citi upgraded to Buy with $278 PT (8x FY27 revenue). Michael Burry reportedly described shorting NBIS as 'shooting fish in a barrel.'

bullets.title: SMCI: +19% on F4Q26 Beat; FY27 Revenue Guided to $65-72B
bullets.body: Super Micro Computer surged ~19% on a substantial EPS and margin beat (gross margin 17.6% in F4Q26) with a $60B backlog and FY27 revenue guidance raised to $65-72B, ahead of Street. Structural gross margin target set at 10%+; no further dilution expected. SpaceX/CRWV exposure cited as key demand driver.

bullets.title: CSCO: Record Q4 Beat, FY27 Guidance Far Above Consensus; AI Orders at $9B
bullets.body: Cisco delivered record Q4 revenue of $17.25B (vs $16.84B est.), EPS $1.22 (vs $1.17 est.), and raised FY27 revenue guidance to $72.2-73.4B vs consensus of $69.12B. AI orders projected at $9B in FY26 with Silicon One and Acacia expansion driving demand. Stock fell initially on lower margin mix from AI hardware vs. software but has rallied +19.2% since May close vs. S&P +4.2%.

bullets.title: LITE: +14% on First $1B Quarter; Laser/EML Demand 30%+ Ahead of Supply
bullets.body: Lumentum achieved its first-ever $1B revenue quarter in F4Q FY26 (+109.3% YoY, +24.5% QoQ) with AI EML and pump laser demand outstripping supply by 30%+. 1.6T transceivers ramping with structural margin expansion. GF Securities added LITE to its preferred list alongside AMD as AI optical infrastructure rebound expected to continue. Wolfe Research hosting earnings takeaway call.

bullets.title: BE: +14% on NBIS $2.6B Master Service Agreement
bullets.body: Bloom Energy surged 14% after Nebius Group disclosed a 10-year, $2.6B master service agreement (signed May) tied to its AI data center buildout. The BE/NBIS commercial relationship signals accelerating demand for fuel-cell power in data center applications.

bullets.title: NVDA: +3% Intraday; GB300 Demand Strong, $1T Market Cap Lead Extends
bullets.body: NVDA rallied ~3% intraday as AI infrastructure backlog data (up 150% YoY to ~$1.7T per JPM), Grok 4.6 launch on GB300 NVL72 hardware, and analyst commentary confirmed sustained GPU demand. Unusual call flow ($1.5M profit on doubled-down whale calls) and NVDA beginning to outperform SOX again. Glassdoor ranked Jensen Huang #1 CEO; NVDA now ~$1T larger than any other public company by market cap.

bullets.title: INTU: Citi Reiterates Buy at $457 PT; FY27 Growth Reset to ~10% Expected to Clear Sentiment
bullets.body: Citi cut FY27/FY28 revenue growth estimates for Intuit to 10.1%/10.7% on softer TurboTax, Mailchimp, and QB Desktop trends. QBO login traffic growth slowed to +2% YoY in July vs. +6% in April; Mailchimp PPC spend down 61% YoY. Stock trades at 17x P/E vs. S&P 20x—cheaper on GAAP basis—with AI tax moats intact. FY27 reset seen as potential clearing event for sentiment.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini Hits 1B MAU; Pixel 11 Launched at $899 with $100 Price Hike
bullets.body: Google Gemini crossed 1 billion monthly active users, the fastest-growing product in company history. Separately, co-founder Brin urged staff to refocus on restoring Gemini to the AI frontier amid unit reorganization. Google launched the Pixel 11 lineup starting at $899 (up $100) with the foldable at $1,899, citing a 'severe memory crunch.' Pixel Watch 5 priced at $399. GOOGL stock touched session lows, down 0.5%, amid broader communication services weakness.

bullets.title: META: $1.4M Unusual Call Buyer at 800 Strike; Open-Weight AI Models Boost Structural Position
bullets.body: An unusual $1.4M call purchase at the 800 strike (37% OTM vs. ~$585) was spotted on META. Separately, Morgan Stanley notes META benefits structurally from open-weight AI models (Muse Spark 1.2 released) shifting value toward compute and inference, maintaining Overweight. META fell ~3.4% on the session per JPM afternoon briefing.

bullets.title: AMZN/GOOGL: MS Overweight on Compute Scarcity; 20-60% ROIC on GB300 Even at Lower Token Prices
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight on AMZN and GOOGL citing lowest-cost-to-serve positioning via custom silicon. Hyperscalers expected to generate 20-60% ROIC on owned GB300 hardware even at ~$1.75/million tokens base case. Open-weight model proliferation benefits hyperscalers via serverless APIs, accelerator rental, RAG/storage, and security services.

bullets.title: CIEN: Outperforming Optical Peers; Flagged as Primary LITE Beneficiary
bullets.body: Ciena outperformed all other optical networking stocks intraday, with an analyst agent flagging it as the primary read-through beneficiary from Lumentum's blowout quarter. CIEN/NOK/CSCO/MRVL highlighted in the scale-across DCI and optical transport theme; Wolfe Research hosting a dedicated earnings-takeaway call covering Ciena, Celestica, Lumentum, and Coherent.

bullets.title: AMD: Added to GF Securities Preferred List; Server CPU Market Seen at $220B by 2030
bullets.body: AMD was added to GF Securities' preferred list alongside LITE as the AI rebound is expected to continue. Analysts see AMD (alongside Arm) continuing to gain server CPU share even as Intel recovers some ground; the server CPU market is modeled to reach ~$220B by 2030. Cerebras-AMD partnership on split prefill/decode architecture also highlighted.

bullets.title: TSLA: Waymo Engineer Perspective on Robotaxi; MS Autonomy Flywheel Tracking
bullets.body: A Waymo engineer shared perspectives on Tesla Robotaxi's strengths and weaknesses over dinner. Morgan Stanley most-read research included post-earnings feedback tracking Tesla's autonomy flywheel and an intern survey showing 'Tesla finding its footing.' Separately, analyst modeled Uber/Tesla capturing 25-50% of Waymo's footprint by 2028 before regulatory cap at 15K vehicles in SF by 2029.

bullets.title: DIS: Iger's Lakers Buy Seen as Commitment Signal; Live 5 Thesis Strengthens
bullets.body: Bob Iger's $12B+ purchase of the LA Lakers with Josh Kushner is interpreted as a signal that Iger is committed to Disney's future rather than reversing course, viewed as positive for new CEO Josh D'Amaro. Morgan Stanley's Live 5 thesis (FWONK, TKO, LYV, SPHR, DIS) frames live events/sports at $50+/hour monetization as protected from AI disintermediation, with DIS parks showing surprise attendance acceleration.

bullets.title: TXN: 1Q Guide Above Seasonal on Industrial Recovery; Auto Growth Mid-Teens YoY
bullets.body: Texas Instruments guided 1Q above seasonal driven by industrial recovery and auto segment contributing mid-teens YoY growth through 2Q (strongest in China). Order trends improving with increasing backlog and stretched lead times; expecting above-seasonal 3Q. Long-term gross margin guidance 75-85%.

bullets.title: SHOP: -2.2% in Canadian Trading; CLS +8.6%
bullets.body: Shopify declined 2.2% in Canadian mid-afternoon trading to C$207.53 while Celestica surged 8.6% to C$469.77, reflecting divergent performance within the tech/AI infrastructure theme.

bullets.title: TSMC CoWoS Yield Hits 99%; ABF Substrate and Memory Remain AI Chip Bottlenecks
bullets.body: TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging yield cleared 99%, but substrate (ABF) lines require $100M-$500M and 18-24 months of investment, while DRAM fabs need $15-20B+ and 3 years—keeping AI chip supply constrained. TSMC called out the ABF shortage itself, and analysts note substrates are expected to clear before DRAM as a constraint.

bullets.title: HOOD: July Customer Growth +80K MoM; Assets $355B Up 19% YoY
bullets.body: Robinhood reported July funded customers at 28.5M (up 80K MoM, 1.77M YoY) and platform assets of $355B (down 4% MoM due to market moves, up 19% YoY). AFRM fell 4.3% alongside fintech/payments sector weakness.

bullets.title: TDS/AD: Citi Maintains Buy; TDS PT $47, AD PT $45 After 2Q26
bullets.body: Citi refreshed models after TDS 2Q results showing TDS Telecom EV contracted to ~4x EBITDA on sum-of-parts; AD trades at 22% premium to exchange offer. Citi downwardly revised TDS Telecom FY26 revenue and EBITDA but raised AD estimates. PT set at $47 TDS and $45 AD with forecast horizon extended to 2035.
